# Adjudication Task — Chapter 969

## Korean source

```text
  1|＃969화
  2|
  3|
  4|
  5|그 찰나의 순간을, 산서인들은 보지 못했다.
  6|
  7|말과 사람의 사체. 거기에 더하여 드문드문 떨어져 있는 바위 틈새를 메운 적들을 온 힘을 다해 밀어붙이느라.
  8|
  9|아니, 설령 가까이에 있었다 해도 아무것도 볼 수 없었을 것이다.
 10|
 11|십왕(十王) 중에서도 세 손가락 안에 꼽히는 초절정 고수의 기감을 속일 만큼 자연스럽고, 쾌속한 일격이었으니.
 12|
 13|서걱!
 14|
 15|마치 타들어 가는 듯한 격통 속, 벽력도왕은 초인적인 인내심으로 허물어지려는 신형을 바로잡았다.
 16|
 17|거대한 쇠망치처럼 뇌리를 후려친, 믿을 수 없는 진실에 몸을 떨며.
 18|
 19|‘그래, 그랬던 것이었나.’
 20|
 21|이제야 알았다. 비로소 깨달았다.
 22|
 23|장성을 넘어 하북을 침략한 젊은 부족장이 살아남을 수 있었던 이유.
 24|
 25|야심에 걸맞은 실력을 지녔었다고는 하나, 그저 뛰어난 유목민에 불과했던 자가 강대한 공력과 초원에서 찾아볼 수 없는 신공절학(神功絶學)을 익힐 수 있었던 이유.
 26|
 27|그날, 자무카는 살아남은 것이 아니었다.
 28|
 29|살려 준 것이다.
 30|
 31|그를 추격하던 모용세가가, 그들을 이끌던 누군가가.
 32|
 33|‘모용백.’
 34|
 35|분노와 고통으로 아득해진 시야 속, 떨리는 손길로 깊숙이 베어진 가슴을 지혈한 벽력도왕은 경악에 물든 눈으로 바라보았다.
 36|
 37|한족과 유목민.
 38|
 39|그 사이 어딘가에 멈춰선 듯한 이국적인 용모의 중년인을.
 40|
 41|“대단하군. 그 상황에서도 용케 반응하다니.”
 42|
 43|고요한 연못처럼 잔잔한 음성.
 44|
 45|그러나 언제 뽑아 들었는지 모를 그의 검은, 이미 섬광 같은 속도로 내리그어지고 있었다.
 46|
 47|쉬익!
 48|
 49|거센 파공성.
 50|
 51|벗이라 믿었던 모용백의 거침없는 일격에, 벽력도왕은 눈을 부릅떴다.
 52|
 53|마지막 순간, 본능적으로 몸을 비틀었던 덕분에 목숨만은 건질 수 있었으나 딱 거기까지다.
 54|
 55|가슴팍을 깊게 훑고 지나간 강기의 여파는, 그의 전신을 물먹은 솜처럼 무겁게 만들었다.
 56|
 57|쾅! 카드드득!
 58|
 59|아슬아슬하게 검신을 가로막은 대도가 휘청인다.
 60|
 61|공력이 흐트러졌음에도 공격을 막아 낸 벽력도왕의 모습에, 모용백이 나직한 탄성을 흘렸다.
 62|
 63|“역시, 무식하기까지 한 그 용력은 여전하군.”
 64|
 65|“모용백, 네놈이 어찌……!”
 66|
 67|벽력도왕은 피가 터지도록 이를 악물었다.
 68|
 69|모용세가와 하북팽가.
 70|
 71|하북팽가와 모용세가.
 72|
 73|천하에 모르는 이가 없는 두 가문이 반목하던 시절이 있었던 것은 사실이다.
 74|
 75|하지만 그것은 과거에 불과했다.
 76|
 77|이미 흐르는 세월과 함께 지나가 버린, 케케묵은 지난날의 흔적.
 78|
 79|그렇기에 벽력도왕은 이 순간에조차 믿어지지 않았다.
 80|
 81|정마대전에서 등을 맞대고 싸웠던 전우가, 젊었을 적의 경쟁자에서 벗이 되어 함께 늙어 간 모용백이 자신을 배신했다는 사실을.
 82|
 83|아니, 이 땅의 모두를 배신했다는 사실을.
 84|
 85|“언제부터. 도대체 언제부터냐.”
 86|
 87|분노와 충격으로 거칠어진 호흡.
 88|
 89|벽력도왕은 파르르 떨리는 날붙이 너머로 보이는 배신자를 향해, 터져 나간 입술을 달싹였다.
 90|
 91|“암천(暗天)과 손을 잡은 것이.”
 92|
 93|그리고 그 물음에 되돌아온 대답은, 더욱 강해진 힘으로 대도를 짓누르는 검신과 그 끝에 실린 강기였다.
 94|
 95|스걱.
 96|
 97|벽력도왕은 터져 나오려는 신음을 삼켰다.
 98|
 99|뜨겁다. 검보다 먼저 살갗에 닿은 모용백의 강기가 그의 쇄골를 파고들고 있었다.
100|
101|조금씩 천천히.
102|
103|쇄골을 이루는 살과 뼈를 가르고, 그 아래 심장 어림에 이를 때까지 멈추지 않을 것처럼.
104|
105|“크아아악!”
106|
107|악문 잇새 사이로 터져 나오는 핏물.
108|
109|벽력도왕은 성난 대호처럼 울부짖으며 대도를 쳐올렸다.
110|
111|분노로 고통을 지워 내고, 하북팽가의 가주에게만 허락된 혼원벽력신공(混元霹靂神功)으로 전신의 모든 공력을 도신으로 쏟아 보냈다.
112|
113|꽈앙!
114|
115|하늘이 쪼개지는 듯한 굉음과 함께 떨어져 나가는 검신.
116|
117|엉망이 된 내부의 혈도와 강기에 의해 갈라진 쇄골에서 끔찍할 정도의 고통이 전해졌으나, 벽력도왕은 강철보다 더한 인내심으로 참아 내며 손을 뻗었다.
118|
119|“놈!”
120|
121|퍼엉!
122|
123|압축된 공기가 터져 나갔다.
124|
125|하북팽가가 자랑하는 절기, 대력금강장(大力金剛掌)의 일 초는 소리조차 앞질러 광포한 기세로 모용백을 휩쓸었다.
126|
127|적어도 아주 잠깐 동안은, 그렇게 보였다.
128|
129|슈확!
130|
131|섬광이 번뜩였고, 그것으로 끝이었다.
132|
133|바람과 함께 쏘아진 장력을 일검에 베어 가른 모용백의 신형이 흐릿해졌다고 느낀 순간, 벽력도왕의 머릿속에 붉은 경고등이 켜졌다.
134|
135|‘이형환위(移形換位)!’
136|
137|쇄골을 지혈할 틈도, 대도를 휘두를 시간도 없다.
138|
139|벽력도왕은 그저 온 힘을 다해 신형을 비틀었다. 찰나의 기척이 느껴진 등 뒤를 향해 돌아서며 일권을 휘둘렀다.
140|
141|후웅.
142|
143|닿았다.
144|
145|살과 뼈로 이루어진 인간의 육신이 아닌, 주먹 끝에서 뭉개지는 바람이.
146|
147|동시에 느꼈다.
148|
149|허공을 후려친 그의 일권 아래에서, 서늘한 살기(殺氣)를 흩뿌리며 쏘아지는 섬광을.
150|
151|“……!”
152|
153|느려진 세상 속, 눈을 부릅뜬 벽력도왕은 이성이 아닌 본능에 따라 움직였다.
154|
155|일평생 품에서 떨어트린 적 없던 대도(刀把)를 놓고, 가슴을 향해 다가오는 섬광을 향해 손을 뻗었다.
156|
157|푸욱.
158|
159|선명하고 느리게 울려 퍼지는 파육음.
160|
161|다급하게 끌어올린 수강(手罡)을 두부처럼 파고든 뾰족한 검 끝이 살과 뼈를 가르고 손등 사이로 고개를 내밀었다.
162|
163|이 정도 장애물은 아무것도 아니라는 듯, 목적지를 향해 계속해서 뻗어 나갔다.
164|
165|터져 나오려는 비명을 억누른 벽력도왕이, 온 힘을 다해 그것을 움켜쥘 때까지.
166|
167|콰드득!
168|
169|그 순간 검이 멈추었다.
170|
171|아니, 정확히는 부서졌다고 해야 옳았다.
172|
173|투둑.
174|
175|핏물과 함께 떨어지는 날붙이의 파편.
176|
177|순식간에 손이 짓이겨지는 그 아득한 고통을 이기지 못한 벽력도왕의 전신이 석상처럼 굳었다.
178|
179|그렇기에 크게 뜨인 눈으로 자신을 바라보는 모용백을, 이내 털끝 하나 다치지 않은 몸으로 일장(一掌)을 내뻗는 그의 모습을 멍하니 지켜볼 수밖에 없었다.
180|
181|화아악.
182|
183|시야를 물들이는 휘황한 빛무리 너머, 모용백의 나직한 음성이 마치 꿈결처럼 흐릿하게 벽력도왕의 귓가에 닿았다.
184|
185|“잘 싸웠네. 투사(鬪士)답게.”
186|
187|그리고.
188|
189|펑.
190|
191|몸속 깊숙한 곳에서 울려 퍼진 한 줄기의 폭발음과 함께, 벽력도왕의 세상이 뒤집혔다.
192|
193|
194|
195|* * *
196|
197|
198|
199|순간, 거대한 진동이 협곡을 휩쓸었다.
200|
201|콰아아아앙!
202|
203|땅이 뒤흔들렸다. 굉음과 함께 암벽의 일부가 무너져 내렸다.
204|
205|언제 만들어진 것인지도 모를 만큼 긴 세월 동안 퇴적된 자연의 산물조차 이럴진대, 피륙으로 이루어진 인간이라면 말할 필요도 없으리라.
206|
207|드드드득!
208|
209|암벽의 일부였던 바위가, 그 위로 엄청난 무게를 지닌 흙과 모래가 쏟아졌다. 동시에 미친 듯이 사방으로 흩날렸다.
210|
211|그러나 한 치 앞도 보이지 않는 희뿌연 먼지구름 속에서도, 모용백은 흔들림 없는 눈동자로 한 곳을 응시하고 있었다.
212|
213|마치 재해(災害)와도 같은 현상을 일으킨 자신의 손을 천천히 그러쥔 채, 반경 수십여 장의 모든 것을 기감으로 받아들였다.
214|
215|지금 막 들썩이는 흙더미 사이로 새어 나온 누군가의 희미한 기침 소리도 역시.
216|
217|쿨럭.
218|
219|모용백은 고개조차 돌리지 않았다. 대신 조용히 손을 뻗어, 소리의 주인을 짓누르고 있던 흙더미의 무게를 덜어 줄 뿐이었다.
220|
221|본래 자신의 것이었던 물건도 함께.
222|
223|우우웅.
224|
225|손짓과 함께 흘러나온 막대한 기운에 공기가 흔들린다. 곧이어 보이지 않는 끈에 당겨지듯, 지면 깊숙이 틀어박혀 있던 한 자루의 창이 그의 손에 붙잡혔다.
226|
227|누군가의 살과 뼈를 관통했다는 증거인, 붉은 선혈을 흘리며.
228|
229|“감사합니다.”
230|
231|등 뒤에서 들려온 자무카의 목소리에, 모용백이 입을 열었다.
232|
233|“왜 내 지시를 따르지 않았나. 분명 최대한 시간을 끌라고 했을 터인데.”
234|
235|“그건…….”
236|
237|“벽력도왕이라는 별호가 우습게 보였나 보군.”
238|
239|뭐라 대답하려던 자무카는 입술을 깨물었다.
240|
241|맞는 말이다. 그는 구원자의 명령을 어겼다.
242|
243|벽력도왕을 상대로도 분전하자 욕심이 생겼고, 합류할 때까지 기다리라는 모용백의 명령을 조금씩 머리에서 지웠다.
244|
245|그리고 한 가지 더.
246|
247|적어도 자신만큼은 잠력단을 사용해선 안 된다는 명령도 함께.
248|
249|“뭐라 드릴 말씀이 없습니다.”
250|
251|“그래, 그럴 테지. 그것을 삼켰다면 지금 이렇게 대화를 나누고 있지도 못했을 테니.”
252|
253|잠력단은 양날의 검이다.
254|
255|적풍단주 풍양을 비롯한 여러 사람의 손에 들어간 초기 단계의 것도 그렇지만, 개량을 거쳐 새롭게 탄생한 잠력단도 엄청난 중독성과 악효과를 지녔다.
256|
257|그러니 한낱 졸(卒)에 지나지 않는 이들이라면 모를까, 대군을 이끄는 총사령관이자 앞으로 해야 할 일이 많은 자무카가 복용해서는 안 되는 일이었다.
258|
259|적어도 그를 전면에 앞세운 모용백의 입장에서는 더더욱.
260|
261|“몸 상태는?”
262|
263|“생각하시는 것만큼 심각하지는 않습니다. 운기(運氣)를 끝마치면 내상은 곧 나아질 듯합니다.”
264|
265|말과는 달리 한쪽 어깻죽지가 거의 반이나 잘려 나가 있는 상태였지만, 도객(刀客)으로서의 생명이 위태로워진 와중에도 자무카의 표정에는 조금도 어둡지 않았다.
266|
267|그는 알고 있었다.
268|
269|자신의 구원자가, 오래전 모용백이 ‘우리’라고 말한 암천이 얼마나 신비롭고 강력한 집단인지.
270|
271|그렇기에 근심 따위는 한 줌도 깃들지 않은 얼굴로 말을 이을 수 있었다.
272|
273|“이제는 구천(九泉)을 떠돌게 생긴 그놈은 저와 다른 처지가 되었지만 말입니다.”
274|
275|그때였다.
276|
277|시종일관 한 방향에 고정되어있던 모용백의 시선이, 자무카로 옮겨간 것은.
278|
279|“아직 멀었군.”
280|
281|“그게 무슨…….”
282|
283|말꼬리를 흐린 자무카가, 순간 앞서 모용백이 했던 말의 의미를 깨닫고 입술을 깨물었다.
284|
285|“그놈이, 벽력도왕이 살아 있다는 말씀이십니까? 아직도?”
286|
287|그의 물음은 당연했다.
288|
289|눈앞에서 똑똑히 보았으니까.
290|
291|일말의 방심도, 자비도 없는 모용백의 손속에 처참하게 무너지던 벽력도왕의 모습을.
292|

*Fwoosh.*

*Poom.*

[P94]
*KABOOM!*

[P95]

[P96]

[P97]
*Krrrrk!*

[P98]

[P99]

[P100]

[P101]

[P102]
*Khk.*

[P103]

[P104]

[P105]
*Wooooom.*

[P107]

[P108]
“Thank you.”

[P110]

[P111]
“Well…”

[P112]
“I suppose you underestimated the Thunderbolt Saber King.”

[P113]

[P114]

[P115]

[P118]

[P127]

*Shhk.*

*Whoooom.*

# Mastering Adjudicator Brief

You are a **veto**, not a second novelist and not a gloss writer.

This call is isolated, non-interactive, and tool-free. The packet already contains the Korean source, both complete English versions, glossary matches, rules, and every numbered hunk. Do not call tools, search the repository, or read files. Do not announce a plan.

The first editor (SOL) has already rewritten the accepted English (BASELINE) for fluency. Default is `SOL`. Take `BASE` only when SOL is actually unfaithful. Write `REPAIR` only when **both** BASE and SOL are unfaithful.

## Default

Choose `SOL` unless a veto below fires.

Keep SOL when it is slangier, punchier, more spoken, or more idiomatic and the Korean sense holds (`기만질` → “con me”, `톡톡히` → “full Peak Master treatment”, `득실거리다` → “crawling with”, `인간 백정` → “butcher of men”, `한 몸` → “are one”, `시원하다` in a bath → “That’s the stuff”, `어렵게 찾아오고 쉽게 깨지는 법` → “hard-won and easily broken”). If SOL already naturalized Korean syntax (`이 혁무진` → “I, Hyuk Mujin”), keep SOL. Do not reproduce Korean word order.

**Literal closeness to Korean wording is not fidelity.** Preserve the source’s meaning and effect in natural English.

## Veto — choose `BASE`

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

* wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action
* a different English idiom than the Korean joke (`까발리다` ≠ “gives someone away”; `넉살` ≠ “banter”)
* a rebuilt joke whose comic machine BASE already has (`얼마나 …는지 …겠다` must stay a simple exaggeration: “snored so loudly even my mother in Ilsan probably heard him,” not “You had to wonder how loudly…”)
* dropped image, attitude, or timing
* SOL replaces an established project rendering, System label, or Markdown convention with an unsupported synonym
* SOL stamps `hyung` (or another kinship title) onto every narrative name when BASE already uses the name and the Korean `형` is ordinary reference, not a vocative or a topical joke (`진호 형` → Jinho in narration)

Do not veto SOL for being informal. Do not veto SOL to “clarify” slang. Do not veto SOL merely because BASELINE is already understandable.

Example: `겹경사가 따로 없다` means two good things **together** (double blessing). `따로` is not “separate.” If BASE says “entirely separate stroke of luck” and SOL says “unexpected windfall,” `REPAIR` to stacked luck.

## Critical binding translation rules

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

## Footnotes

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;
- a deliberately literal rendering whose cultural or linguistic force would otherwise be lost.

For example, render `고시원` as “goshiwon” when the setting or connotations matter, with a concise footnote explaining that it is a very small, inexpensive room-for-rent housing arrangement. Prefer the best natural English analogy in the prose. Use a literal translation plus a concise footnote when the Korean wording itself matters. Define a term at its first meaningful occurrence and do not repeat the note unnecessarily. Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

## Spoilers and Scope

- Safe profiles contain only facts revealed through the latest completed chapter.
- Never read `characters/spoilers/` during drafting. Reviewers may consult one relevant sealed profile only for a specific unresolved continuity issue after the draft is complete.
- Future knowledge may prevent contradiction but may not add early names, pronouns, certainty, motives, or foreshadowing.
- Translate exactly one requested chapter unless the user explicitly requests a batch. Never modify Korean source files under `source/`.

The pointed sword tip drove through the Palm Force he’d hastily summoned as though it were tofu, cut through the flesh and bone of his hand, and emerged from the back of it.

[P77]
As though that obstacle were nothing, it kept driving toward its target.

[P78]
Until the Thunderbolt Saber King, holding back a scream, gripped the blade with all his strength.

[P79]
*Krrrk!*

[P80]
The sword stopped.

[P81]

[P82]
*Plip.*

[P83]
Fragments of the blade fell with his blood.

[P84]
His whole body went rigid under the overwhelming pain of his hand being crushed in an instant.

[P85]
All he could do was stare, eyes wide, at Murong Baek staring back. Then he watched, dazed, as Murong Baek—without so much as a scratch on him—thrust out a palm.

[P86]
*Fwoosh.*

[P87]

[P88]
“You fought well. Like a true warrior.”

[P89]

[P90]
*Poom.*

[P91]

[P92]
* * *

[P93]
A massive tremor swept through the gorge.

[P94]
*KABOOM!*

[P95]
The ground shook. With a thunderous crash, part of the cliff collapsed.

[P96]
Even rock built up by nature over ages too long to measure had given way. A human body of flesh stood no chance.

[P97]
*Krrrrk!*

[P98]
Boulders that had been part of the cliff came crashing down beneath the immense weight of earth and sand above them. Dust and debris flew wildly in every direction.

[P99]
Yet even in the pale cloud, where he couldn’t see a hand in front of his face, Murong Baek kept his eyes fixed on one spot.

[P100]
He slowly closed the hand that had brought about this devastation, taking in everything within several dozen *zhang* through his Qi Sense.

[P101]
Including a faint cough that had just escaped from beneath a shifting mound of earth.

[P102]
*Khk.*

[P103]
Murong Baek didn’t turn his head. He merely reached out and eased the weight of earth pressing down on the person who had coughed.

[P104]
He retrieved something that had once belonged to him as well.

[P105]
*Wooooom.*

[P106]
The air shuddered as immense qi flowed from his gesture. Then a spear buried deep in the ground flew into his grasp as though pulled by an invisible string.

[P107]
Fresh blood ran down it—proof that it had pierced someone’s flesh and bone.

[P108]
“Thank you.”

[P109]
Jamukha’s voice came from behind him. Murong Baek spoke without turning.

[P110]
“Why didn’t you follow my orders? I told you to buy as much time as possible.”

[P111]
“Well…”

[P112]
“I suppose you underestimated the Thunderbolt Saber King.”

[P113]
Jamukha bit his lip instead of answering.

[P114]
Murong Baek was right. He had disobeyed his savior.

[P115]
Holding his own against the Thunderbolt Saber King had made him greedy. Little by little, he had pushed aside Murong Baek’s order to wait for him.

[P116]
And there was one more order he had pushed aside.

[P117]
He, at least, was never to take the Temporary Strength Pill.

[P118]
“I have no excuse.”

[P119]
“No, you don’t. If you’d swallowed it, we wouldn’t be having this conversation.”

[P120]
The Temporary Strength Pill was a double-edged sword.

[P121]
The early versions that had found their way into the hands of Pung Yang, the Red Wind Band Leader, and others were dangerous enough. Even the newly improved pill was highly addictive and carried severe side effects.

[P122]
An ordinary foot soldier might be expendable, but Jamukha was the commander-in-chief of a great army, with much still to do. He could not take it.

[P123]
Not from Murong Baek’s point of view, when he had placed Jamukha at the forefront.

[P124]
“How are you?”

[P125]
“Not as bad as you might think. Once I finish circulating my qi, my internal injuries should heal soon.”

[P126]

[P127]
Jamukha knew how mysterious and powerful his savior’s Dark Heaven was—the Dark Heaven Murong Baek had called “us” long ago.

[P128]
With no worry at all showing on his face, he went on.

[P129]

[P130]

[P131]
“Not yet.”

[P132]
“What do you…?”

[P133]

[P134]

[P135]

[P136]

[P137]
A palm strike of terrifying power had driven him deep into the cliff, where he’d looked like a corpse as he spat blood.

[P138]

[P139]
*Stubborn bastard. Just as always.*

[P140]

[P141]
His natural strength and sturdy body had made him stand out not only within the Hebei Peng Family but among the young prodigies of the entire world. The countless battlefields he had crossed had been no exception.

[P142]
*He always survived. Always.*

[P143]
So Murong Baek intended to end the Thunderbolt Saber King’s life with his own hands.

[P144]

[P145]
The longer his secret remained hidden, the better.

[P146]
Then he could deal another devastating blow to the reinforcements coming from the Nine Sects and One Gang.

[P147]
*At least half a day until Huashan and Zhongnan arrive.*

[P148]
There was still plenty of time.

[P149]
Once everything was ready, Murong Baek would meet the orthodox faction’s reinforcements right here.

[P150]
By then, he would have dealt with the Thunderbolt Saber King. The Hebei Peng Family martial artists beyond the gorge, now falling to the Murong Family’s unexpected ambush, would be dead as well.

[P151]
So would the people of Shanxi, slaughtering nomads on the far side of the suddenly collapsed cliff.

[P152]
First, though, he must not forget the rats hiding beneath the earth, holding their breath.

[P153]
*Shhk.*

[P154]
His spearhead swept through like a streak of light, splitting a huge boulder and the mound of earth beneath it as easily as tofu.

[P155]
Murong Baek looked down impassively at Jin Mukyung, who held the bloodied Cheol Mubaek and Wipeng in his arms.

[P156]
Without a word, he brought his spear straight down.

[P157]
No—he was about to.

[P158]
*Whoooom.*

[P159]
A tremendous rush of air sounded from somewhere, and Murong Baek turned his head on instinct.

[P160]
He saw it.

[P161]
*KABOOOM!*

[P162]
A spear came crashing through, smashing apart the great mass of cliff rock in its path.

[P163]
A blue-white flame burned along its icy, translucent spearhead.

# Mastering Adjudicator Brief

You are a **veto**, not a second novelist and not a gloss writer.

This call is isolated, non-interactive, and tool-free. The packet already contains the Korean source, both complete English versions, glossary matches, rules, and every numbered hunk. Do not call tools, search the repository, or read files. Do not announce a plan.

The first editor (SOL) has already rewritten the accepted English (BASELINE) for fluency. Default is `SOL`. Take `BASE` only when SOL is actually unfaithful. Write `REPAIR` only when **both** BASE and SOL are unfaithful.

## Default

Choose `SOL` unless a veto below fires.

Keep SOL when it is slangier, punchier, more spoken, or more idiomatic and the Korean sense holds (`기만질` → “con me”, `톡톡히` → “full Peak Master treatment”, `득실거리다` → “crawling with”, `인간 백정` → “butcher of men”, `한 몸` → “are one”, `시원하다` in a bath → “That’s the stuff”, `어렵게 찾아오고 쉽게 깨지는 법` → “hard-won and easily broken”). If SOL already naturalized Korean syntax (`이 혁무진` → “I, Hyuk Mujin”), keep SOL. Do not reproduce Korean word order.

**Literal closeness to Korean wording is not fidelity.** Preserve the source’s meaning and effect in natural English.

## Veto — choose `BASE`

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

* wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action
* a different English idiom than the Korean joke (`까발리다` ≠ “gives someone away”; `넉살` ≠ “banter”)
* a rebuilt joke whose comic machine BASE already has (`얼마나 …는지 …겠다` must stay a simple exaggeration: “snored so loudly even my mother in Ilsan probably heard him,” not “You had to wonder how loudly…”)
* dropped image, attitude, or timing
* SOL replaces an established project rendering, System label, or Markdown convention with an unsupported synonym
* SOL stamps `hyung` (or another kinship title) onto every narrative name when BASE already uses the name and the Korean `형` is ordinary reference, not a vocative or a topical joke (`진호 형` → Jinho in narration)

Do not veto SOL for being informal. Do not veto SOL to “clarify” slang. Do not veto SOL merely because BASELINE is already understandable.

## Critical binding translation rules

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

## Footnotes

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;
- a deliberately literal rendering whose cultural or linguistic force would otherwise be lost.

For example, render `고시원` as “goshiwon” when the setting or connotations matter, with a concise footnote explaining that it is a very small, inexpensive room-for-rent housing arrangement. Prefer the best natural English analogy in the prose. Use a literal translation plus a concise footnote when the Korean wording itself matters. Define a term at its first meaningful occurrence and do not repeat the note unnecessarily. Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

## Spoilers and Scope

- Safe profiles contain only facts revealed through the latest completed chapter.
- Never read `characters/spoilers/` during drafting. Reviewers may consult one relevant sealed profile only for a specific unresolved continuity issue after the draft is complete.
- Future knowledge may prevent contradiction but may not add early names, pronouns, certainty, motives, or foreshadowing.

Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

## Footnotes

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;
- a deliberately literal rendering whose cultural or linguistic force would otherwise be lost.

For example, render `고시원` as “goshiwon” when the setting or connotations matter, with a concise footnote explaining that it is a very small, inexpensive room-for-rent housing arrangement. Prefer the best natural English analogy in the prose. Use a literal translation plus a concise footnote when the Korean wording itself matters. Define a term at its first meaningful occurrence and do not repeat the note unnecessarily. Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

- Safe profiles contain only facts revealed through the latest completed chapter.

- Future knowledge may prevent contradiction but may not add early names, pronouns, certainty, motives, or foreshadowing.
